- [`klonick2018new`](../library/klonick2018new.md): (1) J cites Klonick at "pp. 1647–48" and "1664" for the appeals passages. I confirm the audit's corrections: the Facebook appeals sentence is p. 1648, "the lack of an appeals system for individual users" is p. 1665, and J:266 and J:312 should not say 1664. (2) The audit places "a diverse pluralistic group of forces" in the Conclusion; it is in Part IV, p. 1664 (the heading is p. 1649). (3) J:252 lists "reputation and user exit" as one of Klonick's "pluralistic" forces. Klonick treats exit separately and sceptically: Post's "market for rules" is "mostly accurate" for Twitter but misses that users stay and demand change, and platforms are "complementary, not substitute, goods" (pp. 1629–30); on p. 1668 exit sits alongside lobbying as the user's only recourse. (4) J uses Klonick only for the draconian side. She also calls the system "impressively intricate and responsive" (p. 1664), so "draconian" is the facet's word and not hers; her complaint is lack of accountability and unequal treatment, not severity.
- [`mathews1976eldridge`](../library/mathews1976eldridge.md): the J-facet read the due-process passage and quoted the flexibility sentence and the three factors correctly; it noted that the pin cite was missing. The syllabus puts the factors at pp. 332–335. Nothing contradicts the facet.
- [`nagarajrao2026fareshare`](../library/nagarajrao2026fareshare.md): facet J read only the abstract and wrote "178 signups". The body separates 122 users from 178 accounts (pp. 16–17); the abstract's "178 account signups" counts accounts. Facet J's "no outcome data" holds. Its line that the rights "need worker-side tools to be used" overstates: the union had won over 1,400 reactivations and about $3.5 million before the tool (pp. 7, 10), and FareShare automates one bottleneck.
- [`nydfs2015barclays`](../library/nydfs2015barclays.md): the J-facet reading of the recitals, ¶13, ¶24 and ¶25 matches the order. The facet describes the order as dated 18 Nov 2015; the order is signed in November 2015 (day unclear in the scan) and the Department announced it on 18 November.
- [`nydfs2015barclayspr`](../library/nydfs2015barclayspr.md): the J-facet read only the headline paragraphs of the release. The full text matches the facet's quotations and adds nothing that contradicts it.
- [`oomen2016last`](../library/oomen2016last.md): the facet says the paper "contradicts a reading in which last look is simply a dealer privilege". Fully read, the claim is narrower. Under the model, equal effective spreads can be reached by any combination of design and protocol. In the benign-flow case of Figure 8 (§4), Oomen says the designs "can lead to materially different execution risk profiles despite attaining the same effective spread", so the trader's risk is where the rules differ. The equivalence also depends on competing LPs and uninformed flow. The facet gives the published year as 2017, which fits the volume; the bib says 2016, the online date.
- [`oversight2022q1`](../library/oversight2022q1.md): (1) J:246, J:266(iv) and J:316 set "2 decisions" against "about 479,649 submissions". The audit already flagged the cohort mismatch. A second mismatch: one of the two decisions was a Meta referral, so only one of the two comes from the user pool counted in the denominator. (2) "Binding on content" is accurate as J words it; the report's own table shows that policy recommendations are not binding. (3) J:290 says "by Q4 2021" for binding decisions. This report supports "binding decisions" as of Q1 2022; the Q4 2021 report was not read here. (4) J does not use the 70% figure (14 of 20): Meta reversed itself in most shortlisted cases before the Board ruled.
- [`palka2025foreign`](../library/palka2025foreign.md): the facet reads the paper as "terms still contain unfair clauses after the EU consumer-law regime". The text agrees but adds two limits. The comparison is within the EU market, so it says nothing about platform terms elsewhere. EU-headquartered firms were also affected (23 non-Polish EU firms plus 15 Polish).
- [`rosenblat2016algorithmic`](../library/rosenblat2016algorithmic.md): the J-facet cites "soft control (p. 3761)"; the text does use that phrase on p. 3761. The X-facet cites p. 3761 for the argument that the interface serves the interested party; that holds, though the 'neutral intermediary' passage and the soft-control passage share the page. Nothing contradicts the facets. The authors do not test whether disclosure changes driver behaviour.
- [`seattle2024deactivation`](../library/seattle2024deactivation.md): matches the facet's quotations. The facet notes the ordinance text was not found; that is still true here, and this form states only the minimum of what the company must put in the notice. Several of the form's duties (the 90-day window, 14-day response) are given as the company's duties under the ordinance; the ordinance itself is the authority for them.
- [`suzor2016responsibilities`](../library/suzor2016responsibilities.md): the facet says this paper reports fifteen platforms and the 2018 article's abstract says 14, and leaves it unresolved. The full 2018 article (see `suzor2018digital`) names the 14 in its note 3 and says it excluded the Russian-language platform VK from the top 15 by traffic, so the two counts are explained by a change of sample, not an error. This paper does not say why it has 15.
- [`suzor2018digital`](../library/suzor2018digital.md): the facet had this article by abstract only and recorded 14 platforms; the full text confirms 14 and the quoted values. It also shows the sample is 2015 and U.S./common-law centred (p. 4–5), a limit the facet did not carry.
- [`tumey1927ohio`](../library/tumey1927ohio.md): the facet quotation (¶38) and the $12 are right. The facet had read the opinion "in part"; the full text adds the secret-service fund, the mayor's dual role (¶67), the $696.35 and the de minimis limit (¶¶64–65), none of which the facet recorded.
- [`tyler1988what`](../library/tyler1988what.md): the facet says the study "supports the use of the Q2 list as a yardstick for all three settings". The study cuts the other way on one point. Its main finding is that the weights on criteria change with the situation, and its stated conclusion is that no procedure is universally fair (p. 131). The grid needs weights per setting. The facet's list also names "notice", which Tyler did not measure; his items cover representation (process and decision control, p. 111), correctability and the others above. Correctability was measured only as whether the respondent knew of an agency to which they could have complained, and 33% did (p. 113).
- [`us2073usc`](../library/us2073usc.md): the facet recorded (a)(2), (c)(1) and (d) and said it did not find a statutory comment period. That stays true: there is a notice-of-meeting duty, (c)(2), but no comment period. The facet did not record (e), which matters: the process duties are not enforceable by invalidating a rule. A paper citing § 2073 as a model of constrained rule-making should say so.
- [`wong2022meta`](../library/wong2022meta.md): the facet quotes the abstract and reads the Board as "court-like" with Meta controlling jurisdiction and precedent. The text agrees. It adds that the Board's case rulings are binding while its recommendations are not, so "controls" holds most fully for precedent and scope. The text also gives two counts for 2021: 27 decisions (p. 268) and 20 decisions (p. 269), each attributed to the Board's annual report. Do not cite either without checking the report.
## Facet K — Training and cause

- [`dionysius1910composition`](../library/dionysius1910composition.md): the facet's quotation is exact. The facet could not read the page off the scan and put the chapter "between the running heads 265 and 269 by my count"; the chapter runs from p. 251 to p. 270 and the reading passage is on p. 269. The facet's remark that Dionysius "says nothing about word division" is confirmed for the passage.
- [`quintilian1920institutio`](../library/quintilian1920institutio.md): the facet's quotations at 1.1.30, 1.1.32–34 and 1.8.1–2 are correct. Two page corrections from the page markers in this transcription: 1.1.34 sits on p. 37 (the facet gives pp. 37–39), and 1.8.1–2 on p. 147 (the facet gives p. 148). The facet's "read in full" covers 1.1.15–37 and 1.8.1–2; this reading adds 1.7 and 1.5.6.
- [`thrax1874grammar`](../library/thrax1874grammar.md): the facet's quotations (§2 and the footnote) match; the facet read §§1–2 and calls the work "attributed." Davidson (1874) says authenticity "is now generally admitted"; whether that holds against current scholarship was not checked here, so "attributed" is a safe wording.
## Facet X — Counter-case

- [`bucinca2021trust`](../library/bucinca2021trust.md): the full text gives a narrower result. Forcing functions beat simple explanations only on the questions where the AI was wrong, did not raise overall performance, did not differ from each other, and never reached the no-AI level on those questions. "Worked best" holds among the AI conditions on wrong-AI questions only.
- [`cox2016design`](../library/cox2016design.md): the facet's two quotations ("The standard argument is that they [frictions] should be removed from technology in order to reduce the risk of user disengagement"; "The problem with this design approach is that it can also result in mindless forms of interaction that can have negative consequences") are both in the Introduction of the accepted text and match, apart from the bracketed gloss, which is the facet's. The facet's page, 1390, is the proceedings pagination, which this accepted version does not show.
- [`gray2018dark`](../library/gray2018dark.md): facet X (line 95) calls the record "verified, not opened" and cites the paper for the designer as the interested party's instrument. The full text supports "interested party," but the paper does not measure how often designers are the instrument; it says designers "could easily become complicit" and discusses designer character and responsibility (Abstract; pp. 9–10), which is a softer claim than "instrument."
- [`hunt2026decision`](../library/hunt2026decision.md): facet X (line 95) says Gray et al. (2018) is "Part 1's own source for the same point (line 40)". The post's line 40 is as the facet says.
- [`mathur2019dark`](../library/mathur2019dark.md): the facet reads the study from the abstract and introduction. The full text agrees with its figures (1,818 instances, about 11K sites, 22 third parties). It adds the 11.1% prevalence figure, which is a lower bound and a small minority of sites, and the fact that the cognitive-bias links are unvalidated: the authors say these links "may be more nuanced or complex" (§6.4).
- [`plato1925phaedrus`](../library/plato1925phaedrus.md): the facet's quotation (275a) is exact as I read it in the Perseus XML. The words "elixir not of memory, but of reminding" sit in 275a and the clause on "appearance of wisdom" runs into 275b.
- [`vasconcelos2023explanations`](../library/vasconcelos2023explanations.md): the facet file read the abstract only. Its gloss, that cost-lowering helps "when it makes verification cheaper than doing the task", is borne out by Study 1 and Study 2, with two additions the abstract lacks: the effect appeared only in the hard task, and a harder-to-check explanation did no better than no explanation.
## Facet Z — Gap search

- [`appleton2023sketchbook`](../library/appleton2023sketchbook.md): the facet says summary only and "No history analogy." The full page agrees; it adds that the design aim is to keep the writer's own reasoning active, which the facet does not state.
- [`buschek2024collage`](../library/buschek2024collage.md): the facet's reading from the abstract ("adjacent in method, distant in content") holds. The full text adds that his history is literary Expressionism and Manovich's 1999 "avant-garde as software" (with hyperlinking as a parallel), and that he explicitly limits the claim to interface form.
- [`butskhrikidze2022what`](../library/butskhrikidze2022what.md): the facet file read the abstract and filed the paper as a technical NLP/DH use of the term. The full text shows it is a linguistic-typology paper, not NLP, though it matches the facet's verdict that it concerns living unspaced scripts and not an analogy.
- [`cho2021giving`](../library/cho2021giving.md): the facet says the abstract "mentions *scriptio continua* only as the contrast case". The body does the same and no more (Section 1, p. 2; Section 2, p. 3 on "indecisive spacings" in Chinese, Japanese and Korean). The facet's "literal, not analogical" is right.
- [`clerice2020evaluating`](../library/clerice2020evaluating.md): the facet file read the abstract and listed it as a technical use of the term. The full text bears that out. It adds the dating sentence above, which the abstract does not show.
- [`cordeiro2026control`](../library/cordeiro2026control.md): the facet (line 289) says "journalism; 'democratic legibility' as the capacity to read information systems" from the abstract. The full text confirms that, and adds that it is a programme statement for a newsletter, not a study or paper; the facet and bib call it an essay, which is fair.
- [`dasgupta2023designing`](../library/dasgupta2023designing.md): the facet describes the paper as "designing for learners' literacies" from the record only. The full text confirms that and shows the learners are children and the evidence is the authors' own case work.
- [`dembeck2023flow`](../library/dembeck2023flow.md): the facet's summary, quotations and sections match the text. It rightly flags the single algorithm mention.
- [`fujii2023how`](../library/fujii2023how.md): the facet file read the abstract and filed the paper under "tokenization of unspaced scripts (Japanese, Thai, Old French and Latin)... not an analogy". Japanese only was tested here; Thai and Chinese appear only in the introduction's list, and the authors name other languages as future work (p. 43). The facet's conclusion otherwise stands.
- [`koomen2025horseless`](../library/koomen2025horseless.md): the facet says the email scenario involves a boss as recipient, not as a party the mediator reads. The text bears that out: Koomen's agent reads his own inbox and drafts as him. The facet's "only neighbour with an agent acting for a person" is a fair reading of what I saw, but I did not survey others.
- [`lermannhenestrosa2026human`](../library/lermannhenestrosa2026human.md): facet Z (lines 284, 368) summarises it from the abstract as an institutional remedy, "no history of reading; no triad; none addresses Nadella." The full text agrees. It also says that general-purpose AI users are not served by "AI literacy" alone (§3.3), which is close to ruling D3, but it makes the point for regulatory reasons.
- [`litt2025malleable`](../library/litt2025malleable.md): the facet (summary only) says "one person and their tools" and "no history analogy." The full text confirms the missing history but contradicts "one person": a whole section ("Communal creation") argues that malleability is a group matter, with shared tools for teams, hospital departments and Mastodon instances.
- [`nielsen2023paradigm`](../library/nielsen2023paradigm.md): the facet's account matches the text. The phrase "articulation barrier" is not in this article; it is the title of a different Nielsen piece listed in the "More on AI UX" series (confirming the facet's note).
- [`oeldorfhirsch2023what`](../library/oeldorfhirsch2023what.md): the facet recorded this as a Crossref record "not read" and grouped it among literacy-critique sources. The facet's claim that none of these says "literacy is the wrong frame" for the triad holds for this review: it extends the frame and does not question it.
- [`wattenberger2023chatbots`](../library/wattenberger2023chatbots.md): the facet (Z, entry for this key) says "No writing-history analogy" and describes one user and a tool. The full text agrees on both. It adds that she wants the interface to carry the user's burden, which is the same direction as the paper's spacing precedent; the difference is scale and parties. The essay models one user and one chatbot and never mentions an interested third party, so it does not bear on the triad (rulings D8, D9).
- [`zhu2026designing`](../library/zhu2026designing.md): facet Z (entry 16) quoted the abstract line about designing outputs so humans can check and contest them "without having to resolve the task," and concluded that "none of these sources replaces the human check with structure." The abstract quote is accurate. The conclusion needs a qualifier for this paper: Zhu keeps the human as evaluator at run time, but pushes much of the checking to design time and to sampling (pp. 5-6), so structure does replace some run-time checks. The paper does not ask what task the person keeps once the structure is in place; it asks how to make the person's check cheaper.
